items.title: RT Madison Mills: SCOOP: Major U.S. banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents inside customer accounts, including some attempting to take...
items.description_html:
RT Madison Mills
SCOOP: Major U.S. banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents inside customer accounts, including some attempting to take actions that appear to be independent of user instructions, sources told Axios.

The findings have alarmed banking executives, who are racing to restrict access to their systems as AI moves at a velocity faster than financial institutions can respond, multiple industry and bank executives told Axios.

Several banks are now preparing for worst-case and even “day after” scenarios, including how to rapidly secure or restore customer accounts if things go wrong, the people said.

Several bank executives told Axios they're struggling to distinguish between human users and AI agents. One executive said banks also struggle to determine whether agents are authorized by customers or potentially operating without their permission, more akin to rogue agent behavior.

Read my latest for Axios here: https://www.axios.com/2026/10/22/ai-agents-banks-unauthorized-accounts-access

items.title: RT Tijori: Saudi Arabia is reducing oil cargoes to European refiners. Oil being cut off has happened to Europe before, Abqaiq (2019) and the 2022 Russ...
items.description_html:
RT Tijori
Saudi Arabia is reducing oil cargoes to European refiners. Oil being cut off has happened to Europe before, Abqaiq (2019) and the 2022 Russia Disruption

At that time Indian refiners who benefitted massively were RIL, MRPL AND CPCL

RIL — the big direct winner. Most of what it makes is transport fuel, and the SEZ refinery is built to export.

MRPL — exports ~40% of its output, and half its slate is diesel + ATF. Exactly what Europe will be short of.

-CPCL is an indirect beneficiary. Products transferred from CPCL to parent IOCL are billed on an import-parity pricing (IPP) basis. When international product benchmarks and cracks increase, CPCL's realized refinery-gate prices rise immediately, boosting standalone GRM and operating cash flows.

items.title: Muthoot Finance holds nearly 200 tonnes of gold as collateral. To put that number in perspective, if Muthoot were ranked alongside countries by centra...
items.description_html:
Muthoot Finance holds nearly 200 tonnes of gold as collateral.

To put that number in perspective, if Muthoot were ranked alongside countries by central bank gold reserves, it would sit at roughly 25th globally.

Singapore: ~200 tonnes
Muthoot Finance: ~200 tonnes
Brazil: ~175 tonnes
Pakistan: ~65 tonnes

In other words, Muthoot has custody of roughly 3× as much gold as Pakistan’s central bank holds in reserves.

Of course, Muthoot doesn’t own this gold—it is pledged by borrowers. But the sheer scale of the collateral sitting in its vaults is remarkable.

items.title: Modi Says Buy Less Gold. Imports Crash 81%. Coincidence? In May, PM Modi urged Indians to avoid unnecessary gold purchases. In September, he repeated ...
items.description_html:
Modi Says Buy Less Gold. Imports Crash 81%. Coincidence?

In May, PM Modi urged Indians to avoid unnecessary gold purchases. In September, he repeated the appeal.

Meanwhile, gold import duties jumped from 6% to 15%.

September imports collapsed to just $1.8 billion down 81% YoY.

High prices, domestic recycling and government policy are all potentially reshaping demand.

But here's the bigger question: Is Modi's appeal actually changing India's gold-buying behaviour, or are economics doing the heavy lifting?

For India, the implications extend beyond jewellery to the trade deficit, forex reserves and rupee.

India's draft Defence Acquisition Procedure (DAP 2026) sends a strong message to defence companies:

🔹 The standalone Buy (Indian) procurement route disappears.

🔹 Indigenous design retains top priority, while technology transfer and local manufacturing gain importance.

items.title: Same Country. Same Sovereign Risk. But Its 10-Year Bonds Look Expensive While Its 30-Year Bonds Look Cheap. MS's sovereign bond analysis reveals an in...
items.description_html:
Same Country. Same Sovereign Risk. But Its 10-Year Bonds Look Expensive While Its 30-Year Bonds Look Cheap.

MS's sovereign bond analysis reveals an interesting divergence.

Saudi Arabia, Poland, Mexico, Turkey, Romania and Indonesia all show cheap 30Y versus rich 10Y classifications.

Bahrain, Oman and Uruguay show the opposite.

Here's what interests me as an investor:

The opportunity may not be in choosing which country's bonds to buy, but in choosing which maturity offers better compensation for risk.

Credit ratings tell us which countries are risky.

But the spread curve may tell us where the market is mispricing that risk.

The real question: Are these maturity divergences justified by long-term credit risks, or are they relative-value opportunities hiding in plain sight?

items.title: RT Exencial Research Partners: “Resilient to Higher Rates”? Or Is the Market Simply Hiding the Damage? US 10-year Treasury yields have risen nearly ...
items.description_html:
RT Exencial Research Partners
“Resilient to Higher Rates”? Or Is the Market Simply Hiding the Damage?

US 10-year Treasury yields have risen nearly 100 bps in 2026. Yet Wall Street remains near record highs.

MS raises an important question: At what point do higher interest rates actually become a problem for equities?

The answer isn't as simple as most investors think.

Higher rates aren't necessarily bearish. What matters is WHY they're rising.

If yields rise because economic growth is accelerating, stronger corporate earnings can offset higher borrowing costs.

But if yields rise because inflation is returning or central banks are tightening excessively, the equation changes.

And here's the interesting part.

While headline indices appear resilient:

🔹 Over half the Russell 3000 has experienced a 20%+ drawdown since June.

🔹 US CCC credit spreads have widened 400 bps YTD.

🔹 AI giants continue investing aggressively, while leveraged businesses struggle with financing costs.

The market isn't immune to higher rates. Its strongest companies are simply absorbing the shock better than the weakest.

items.description_html:
RT Exencial Research Partners
India’s Next Bull Market May Be Built in Factories, Not Trading Screens! 🇮🇳

Everyone is chasing AI stocks. But look at India's upcoming investment pipeline:

🔹 ₹5.27 lakh crore - Semiconductors
🔹 ₹5.07 lakh crore - Defence
🔹 Up to $200 billion - Data centres
🔹 Over $70 billion - AI

Impressive numbers. But as an investor, I look at three things:

1. Capital Committed - What's announced.
2. Capital Deployed - What actually gets spent.
3. Shareholder Returns - What generates profits, free cash flow and ROCE.

The market celebrates the first, anticipates the second and often forgets the third.

India’s Growth Story Is Intact. Its Stock Market Premium Isn't.

For years, global investors were willing to pay almost any price for India's growth story. That enthusiasm is now being tested.

India's valuation premium over emerging markets has fallen to ~60%, against a long-term average of ~80%.

Meanwhile, much of India's post-Covid market outperformance has evaporated in USD terms.

As global money chases AI opportunities elsewhere, India is no longer the obvious EM favourite.

But here’s the interesting part.

India hasn't necessarily become cheap. It has become relatively less expensive.

items.title: Zetwerk is among the first venture backed, manufacturing-focused tech platforms from India’s startup ecosystem to go public. Kae Capital (along with ...
items.description_html:
Zetwerk is among the first venture backed, manufacturing-focused tech platforms from India’s startup ecosystem to go public.

Kae Capital (along with affiliate Kalysta Capital) is the standout winner. It invested at an average cost of just Rs 3.94 a share.

At Zetwerk’s Rs 151 IPO price, that translates into a 38x return.

It has sold shares worth over Rs 253 crore, and will collectively hold 3.33% stake worth Rs 868 crore.

Other early investors have also done well.

Peak XV Partners: Making about 24x return. Sold shares worth Rs 266 crore and retaining a 7.1% stake worth ~Rs 1,849 crore.

Peak holds another 2.4% stake through late stage funds, and will make about 3x.

Accel India: Making 19x return, selling Rs 181 crore and retaining 6.2% stake worth Rs 1,611 crore.

Lightspeed India: About 11x return, selling Rs 175 crore and retaining 2.7% stake worth Rs 693 crore.

Lightspeed later funds hold 4.5% stake, and will make about 3x.

But the biggest institutional shareholder is taking a very different approach.

Greenoaks is not selling a single share in the IPO.

Across four entities, it owns nearly 20% pre-IPO, making it Zetwerk’s largest shareholder.

After dilution, Greenoaks will still own about 17.5%, worth roughly Rs 4,557 crore at the IPO price.


The Arc: 🚨 Zetwerk was listed on Friday, with its share price opening at a 5% premium to IPO price of Rs 151 before slipping into red.

Current market cap stands at Rs 24,900 crore.

The Rs 5,012 crore IPO was subscribed 3x earlier this week.

items.description_html:
RT Pratik Bhakta
Back to Twitter after a short break!!

Today I have a story on IDfy, an identity verification startup.

Around 2023-24, IDfy shifted away from the video-KYC API business to build a full-stack identity verification and customer onboarding suite.

Its target: Banks, BFSI firms, ecommerce, logistics companies.

2026: The company is profitable, scaling fast, growing internationally and aiming an IPO in the next 2 years. (Details in the story)

But there is a catch. This is a business where margins are perpetually under a squeeze. Competition is intense. And AI is a game changer.

So how can IDfy create a differentiated proposition? And stay ahead of competition?

Read all the details in my latest story, link in the comment below.

items.title: Swiggy’s founder Sriharsha was asked about the market cap and execution gap as compared to Eternal and investing more aggressively on the earnings ca...
items.description_html:
Swiggy’s founder Sriharsha was asked about the market cap and execution gap as compared to Eternal and investing more aggressively on the earnings call yesterday.

His response.

“I think our competitor, Blinkit, enjoys a pretty strong flywheel that has been compounding over the years. That is the reason why they’ve been able to build a more resilient business........I think our first job is to build a stable, resilient business that has clearest line of sight to EBITDA zero. The optionalities come after that.”

Blinkit was about 1.7x of Instamart in terms of net order value (NOV) back in mid 2024.

Now that gap is 3.2x.

More on what the execution gap between Blinkit and Instamart looks like over the last 10 quarters...


Madhav Chanchani: Swiggy's share price is down by 5% today, hitting an all time low.

Eternal's market cap is now 5x of Swiggy (Rs 2.96 lakh crore vs 58,000 crore).

It was just a little over 2x when Swiggy went for an IPO in Nov 2024.

items.title: Some interesting observations from Deepinder Goyal on impact of AI agents on commerce from Eternal’s shareholder letter - He sees some potential risk...
items.description_html:
Some interesting observations from Deepinder Goyal on impact of AI agents on commerce from Eternal’s shareholder letter

- He sees some potential risk from agents for District, where they can go “around the platform and go direct.”

Feels in both food delivery and quick commerce the company controls supply chain and infrastructure to retain margins.

- “An agent is a more demanding customer than a human: it optimises each transaction on actual outcomes, not habit or brand loyalty, and routes to whichever platform is objectively better at that moment. In categories with overlapping supply, this compresses the market toward the execution leader.”

- Sees opportunities to expand into categories where user content like reviews, ratings, curated lists have been a moat.




Madhav Chanchani: Deepinder Goyal is making an AI play at Eternal.

Dark will be built on "fine-tuned frontier open-weight models" with privacy being its key differentiator.

It is being built for founders, researchers, scientists, enterprises and governments.
